Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  - 2 months of low energy/fatigue, difficulty getting up, reduced appetite, difficulty sleeping, impaired concentration/distractibility, lower mood, decreased sex drive, and exertional shortness of breath during sports. - Known hypothyroidism.
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  - Father died by suicide ~15 years ago. - Mother well. - No other family psychiatric or medical history reported.
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  - Thyroxine (levothyroxine) – dose/route/frequency not documented. - No known drug allergies.
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  - Married. - Decreased libido over the past few months. - Morning erections: initially reported not noticing them recently; later stated no change (conflict noted). - No other sexual health concerns recorded.
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  - Engages in sports; notes increased shortness of breath with exertion. - Diet: reduced appetite. - Tobacco, alcohol, and other substances: Not recorded.
- Hearing and vision concerns:  - Vision: no changes reported. - Hearing: Not recorded.
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  - Lower mood for ~2 months; difficulty sleeping; low energy; reduced appetite; impaired concentration; decreased interest/libido. - Denies suicidal or homicidal thoughts. - No prior mental health diagnoses reported.
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  - Married. - Started a new job ~2 months ago (temporal association with symptom onset). - No housing/financial or caregiving issues recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary: Adult with known hypothyroidism on levothyroxine presents with ~2 months of fatigue, insomnia, low mood, reduced appetite, impaired concentration, decreased libido, and new exertional dyspnea temporally associated with starting a new job. Denies suicidality. No exam or labs obtained in this encounter. Plan made for in-person evaluation and blood tests with GP in the next few days.
- Relevant differentials (consistent with transcript and DDx):
  - Depressive disorder vs adjustment disorder with depressed mood: multiple depressive symptom domains with temporal link to job change.
  - Thyroid dysfunction (under- or over-replacement): symptoms overlap with hypo- and hyperthyroid effects; patient on levothyroxine.
  - Anemia: fatigue and exertional dyspnea.
  - Primary insomnia/stress-related sleep disturbance contributing to daytime symptoms.
  - Hypogonadism: decreased libido; morning erections history conflicting.
- Working diagnosis: Depressive symptoms likely consistent with adjustment disorder vs major depressive disorder, with contributing insomnia; rule out thyroid dysfunction and anemia given history and symptoms.
- Considerations: Hypogonadism if libido symptoms persist after addressing mood/thyroid; less likely cardiopulmonary pathology given subacute course and absence of red flags in transcript.
- Plan from visit: Arrange in-person examination and blood tests via GP within the next few days; further investigations to be guided by clinical assessment.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Major depressive disorder vs adjustment disorder with depressed mood – Likelihood: High. Justification: 2 months of low mood, insomnia, fatigue, reduced appetite, impaired concentration, and decreased interest/libido temporally associated with starting a new job; denies suicidality.
- Thyroid dysfunction related to hypothyroidism or levothyroxine dosing – Likelihood: Medium. Justification: Known hypothyroidism on levothyroxine with symptoms compatible with under- or over-replacement; requires thyroid function testing.
- Anemia (iron deficiency or other) – Likelihood: Medium. Justification: Fatigue and new exertional shortness of breath over months; needs CBC and iron studies.
